title: History of Sidi Nu'uman
summary: The young gentleman who had been seen grooming his mare with mingled tears and reprimands bowed before the Caliph and introduced himself as Sidi Nu'uman.
full_text:
The young gentleman who had been seen grooming his mare with mingled tears and reprimands bowed before the Caliph and introduced himself as Sidi Nu'uman.

'Commander of the Faithful,' he said, 'the mare in my stable is no ordinary beast; she was once Aminah, my treacherous wife, who practiced forbidden sorcery.

When I married her, she was reputed to be a woman of modesty and noble lineage. Yet at our dining table, she behaved most unnaturally: instead of eating our meals, she would pick up grains of rice one by one with a tiny ivory bodkin. Suspecting an eerie mystery, I pretended to fall asleep one night, only to follow her stealthily out of the city gates.

To my horror, I tracked her to a desolate graveyard, where she communed with ghouls under the pale crescent. When I confronted her the following dawn and demanded she repent her profane ways, her face contorted with wicked fury. She dipped a cup of water, threw the spray into my face, and pronounced a terrible curse:
"Quit the shape of man and take the form of an outcast dog!"

Instantly my bones cracked, my posture dropped upon four paws, and I barked in agony. Driven out of my own home, I wandered the alleys, hunted by butcher boys and starved near gutters. Yet my human intellect remained trapped within the canine shell.

One day, I sought refuge inside the bakery of a kind-hearted man. Seeing my gentle eyes, he tossed me a loaf of bread, which I ate with clean, orderly manners. Astonished, the baker adopted me as his watchman. Soon after, a woman came into the shop and tried to pay with counterfeit silver coins. Recognizing the deception, I leaped up, pinned the woman's robe with my paws, and overturned the bad money!

A learned lady passing by observed my discernment. She was a practitioner of white magic and lawful wisdom. She whispered to the baker:
"This is no dog, but an honorable man ensorcelled by a malevolent sorceress!"

She brought me to her home, prepared a bowl of consecrated spring water, and cast the counter-spell upon my head. My limbs straightened, my voice returned, and I knelt in tearful thanksgiving. She then gave me a flask of magical dew and said:
"Go back to thy house. Cast this upon thy treacherous wife and pronounce her punishment."

I strode into my home, took Aminah by surprise, and threw the water upon her, commanding: "Leave the form of woman and become a mare, bearing burdens as a beast of toil!"

Thus she became the mare. Every morning I tend her with good grain and clean straw out of humane duty, but I reprove her sternly to remind her spirit of the wickedness that stripped her of humanity.'

Caliph Harun al-Rashid marveled at the divine balance of justice, granting Sidi Nu'uman honors and protection throughout the empire.
moral: Deceit and sorcery unravel before courage and righteousness, restoring dignity to those who uphold honor.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
